items.context: backlog/batch_handler.go is the single worst complexity offender at complexity_max 59 — far beyond the next worst (files.go at 35). This likely contains a deeply nested function with many branches. The decomposition strategy will set the pattern for other production files.

options.label: Extract each batch operation into its own named function in the same file
options.rationale: Break the high-complexity function into smaller named functions (e.g., batchValidate, batchApplyStatus, batchApplyPriority). Keep everything in batch_handler.go but make each function focused. Simplest change, lowest risk, directly reduces complexity_max. Recommended because it's the most targeted fix.

options.label: Split into multiple files by batch operation type
options.rationale: Create batch_handler_status.go, batch_handler_priority.go, etc. Reduces both file length and complexity. More structural change but better organization long-term.

items.topic: Execution ordering: phases or interleaved by package?
items.context: The plan has 5 sequential phases (extract utilities → decompose production → split tests → cleanup → verify). An alternative is to work package-by-package (all backlog/ changes first, then ideas/, then execution/, etc.). Package-by-package allows running tests for a single package after each batch, catching regressions faster. Phase-by-phase keeps similar refactoring types together.

options.label: Keep phase-based ordering as written
options.rationale: Phase 1 (shared utilities) must come first since later phases depend on fileserve/testutil. After that, phases 2-3 group similar work types which is more systematic. Recommended because the fileserve dependency makes pure package-ordering impractical anyway.

options.label: Phase 1 first, then interleave by package
options.rationale: After shared utilities are extracted, work through each package completely (production + tests together). Tighter feedback loops per package. More context-switching but easier to reason about per-package correctness.

items.context: With 30 files to refactor, the commit strategy affects both safety (rollback granularity) and efficiency (commit overhead). Options range from one commit per file to batching by phase.

options.label: One commit per logical refactor unit (small groups of related files)
options.rationale: E.g., one commit for the entire fileserve extraction (3 files + new package), one commit per production file split, one commit per test file split. Balances granularity with practicality. Recommended because it provides meaningful rollback points without excessive commit overhead.

options.label: One commit per file
options.rationale: Maximum granularity. Easy to bisect. But 30+ commits is noisy and some changes (like fileserve extraction) span multiple files atomically.

options.label: One commit per phase
options.rationale: Fewest commits but hard to rollback individual changes if one file's refactor causes issues.

items.freeform: You are not allowed to perform commits. I do that manually

items.topic: Score target adjustment given reduced scope
items.context: Round 2 d1 selected 'target top-30 files, accept partial improvement'. The original target was >=70. With CLI excluded and only 30 of 100+ files in scope, the achievable score is uncertain. The top 30 files include the worst offenders (complexity 59, 35, 35, 29, 29, 28, 24, 20...) which disproportionately affect scores. However, the remaining 70+ files still contribute violations.

options.label: Target >=50, measure and iterate
options.rationale: Set >=50 as the primary target. After executing, measure the actual score. If it's close to 70, do a quick pass on additional easy wins. If far below, create a follow-up item. Recommended because it's pragmatic — the top 30 files hold the most extreme violations.

options.label: Keep >=70 target, expand scope if needed during execution
options.rationale: Start with 30 files but allow the executing agent to add more files if the score is tracking below 70. Risk: scope creep makes the item too large.

options.label: No score target, just address the 30 files
options.rationale: Focus on completing the file list rather than hitting a number. Score improvement is a side effect. Simple success criteria but less measurable.
